newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures extend short-covering gains.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures extend short-covering gains.

text.p: CME lumber futures were sharply higher near midsession on continued short covering after recent limit declines, traders said.
The recent declines put the July contract at a discount to cash prices, which prompted the short covering, traders said.

Trading limits were expanded to $15.00 per thousand board feet following the two limit losses. Traders said futures were well oversold in comparison to the cash equivalent and this prompted the shortcovering, traders said.
Cash spruce is reportedly in the $345 to $350 per tbf area for mill asking prices.
At 1036 CDT, lumber was up $8.00 to $2.00 per tbf with July up $6.90 at $354.00 per tbf and September was up $8.00 at $352.00.
